svg.text: Standard Hub-and-Spoke Without Bow-Tie: C1 vs. Region A Failure
Failure Outcome A: C1 Peering Outage (Region A Workloads Still Up)
- Connected MPLS: Region A UNREACHABLE over ER (unless NVA/ARS global transit exists).
- Region B Access: Branch 1 -> MPLS -> Branch 2 -> C2 -> HUB 2 stays online.
- Isolated Branch 1 (No MPLS): Loses BOTH Region A & Region B (Global Reach at C1 down).
- Verdict: Single peering-site failure disconnects healthy Region A workloads from on-prem.
B. Full Azure Region A Outage
Failure Outcome B: Full Azure Region A Outage (Peering C1 Healthy)
- Orphaned Circuit: Healthy C1 has no VNet connection to HUB 2 in Region B!
- MPLS Saturation: Branch 1 hauls 100% of DR traffic via MPLS -> Branch 2 -> C2 -> HUB 2.
- Isolated Branch 1 (No MPLS): CUT OFF from Region B DR unless Global Reach (C1<->C2) is ON!
- Global Reach Rescue: Global Reach C1 <-> C2 lets C1 transit MSEE backbone to C2 -> HUB 2.
Azure Networking Field Architect Handbook | Part 3: Hybrid Connectivity
